Feature · Issue 31

The cartographers of fog

Three surveyors, one coastline that refuses to stay put, and the maps they keep redrawing anyway.

By our coastal correspondent · 34 min

On the morning the fog came in for good, the survey team had already measured the bay four times. Each time the shore had moved: not far, a stride or two, but enough to make a liar of every map in the harbour office.

“A map is a promise. The sea has never signed one.”

The eldest of the three keeps the old sheets in a drawer that sticks. She does not throw them away. She calls them drafts, as if the coast were still deciding what it wanted to be.

The harbour master would prefer a final version. He has asked for one every spring for eleven years, and every spring he receives a polite letter explaining, at some length, why the sea has other plans.
